brass_key.name: Brass key
brass_key.description: Heavy and cold. A tag reads: TOWER DOOR. The tag is stamped with a small seal: an anchor with an open eye.

oil_lantern.name: Oil lantern
oil_lantern.description: Still half full. It throws a warm, steady light.

cottage.title: The Keeper's Cottage
cottage.text: Rain hammers the windows of Keeper Elena Vos's cottage. She has not lit the lighthouse for three nights, and no one has seen her. Her tea is cold on the table. A writing desk sits in the corner, the shore path leads down to the water, and the cliff path climbs toward the dark lighthouse.

actions.label: Search the writing desk
actions.message: You pull out the creaking chair and sit at the desk.

actions.label: Walk down to the shore
actions.message: You follow the slippery path down to the boathouse.

actions.label: Climb the cliff path to the lighthouse
actions.message: Wind tears at your coat as you reach the foot of the tower.

desk.title: The Writing Desk
desk.text: Papers, tide tables and a leather logbook cover the desk. Three nights in the tide tables are circled in pencil. A page has been torn out of the logbook. One drawer is slightly open.

notes.text: Something brass glints inside the open drawer.
The drawer is empty now. You already took the key.
The torn-out page came right after 'Tell the harbor master.' Her pen pressed through to the page beneath, and two words still show: 'old watchtower'.

actions.label: Take the key from the drawer
actions.message: You take a heavy brass key. Its tag reads: TOWER DOOR. The tag is stamped with a small seal: an anchor with an open eye.

actions.label: Read the last entry in the logbook
actions.message: Elena's handwriting shakes: 'The lights aren't for ships anymore. The man with the red boat signals someone out at sea. If I vanish, do NOT trust him. Tell the harbor master.'

actions.label: Go back to the cottage
actions.message: You leave the desk and return to the middle of the room.

shore.title: The Boathouse
shore.text: Waves slam against the jetty. An old oil lantern hangs on a hook by the boathouse door. Across the bay, the harbor master's window glows.

notes.text: A fisherman in a yellow coat is tying up a red boat.
The hook by the door is empty. The lantern is with you.
The fisherman gives you a thin smile. 'I'll keep an eye on the tower for you.'
After a while, the harbor master's window goes dark, then lights again. Your message got through. Moments later, the red boat slips away from the jetty with no lights showing.

actions.label: Take the oil lantern
actions.message: You lift the lantern off its hook and light it. It burns steadily.

actions.label: Tell the fisherman that the keeper is missing
actions.message: 'Missing, you say?' He glances up at the tower. 'Leave it with me. Don't you go up there tonight.' He walks off quickly toward the red boat.

actions.label: Say nothing to him and send a note to the harbor master
actions.message: You give a boy a coin to run your note across to the harbor master: 'Watch the lighthouse tonight.' The fisherman watches you but says nothing.

actions.label: Tell no one what you know
actions.message: You keep what you know to yourself. The fisherman never looks your way. To him you are just a stranger passing through.

actions.label: Climb back up to the cottage
actions.message: You climb back up the path, rain in your eyes.

tower_door.title: Foot of the Lighthouse
tower_door.text: The lighthouse rises above you into the storm. A heavy iron door blocks the way in.

notes.text: The brass key in your pocket feels like it would fit the lock.

actions.label: Unlock the iron door
actions.blocked_message: The door is locked tight. You need a key.
actions.message: The brass key turns with a groan. The door swings open onto blackness.

actions.label: Return to the cottage
actions.message: You head back to the cottage, out of the wind.

stairwell.title: The Stairwell
stairwell.text: A spiral staircase climbs into complete darkness. Somewhere above, something thumps against the floor. Parts of the stairs look broken.

notes.text: Your lantern shows where the steps are broken.

actions.label: Climb the stairs
actions.blocked_message: It is far too dark. You would fall through the broken steps. You need a light.
actions.message: Holding the lantern high, you step over the gaps and climb toward the thumping.

actions.label: Go back outside
actions.message: You step back out into the rain.

lamp_room.title: The Lamp Room
lamp_room.text: At the top you find Keeper Elena Vos, tied to a chair next to the great lamp. She has been kicking the floor for help. 'He'll be back soon,' she whispers. 'The fisherman. He uses my light to guide the smugglers in.' Below, you hear an engine. A red boat is heading for the jetty.

actions.label: Light the great lamp and flash the harbor-alarm pattern
actions.blocked_message: You could flash the lamp, but no one ashore is watching for a signal. You never warned the harbor.
actions.message: The beam sweeps across the bay: long, short, long. The harbor master has been watching, and within minutes the coastguard's siren answers.

actions.label: Untie Elena and hide with her in the dark
actions.message: You cut Elena free and crouch behind the lamp. Footsteps come up the stairs, and then a key turns in the lock below.

ending_rescue.title: Ending: The True Keeper
ending_rescue.text: Blue lights fill the jetty. The coastguard arrests the fisherman while he is still tying up his red boat. Elena wraps a blanket around your shoulders. 'You read the signs,' she says. 'Maybe the light should be yours now.' Plot twist: the helpful stranger was the smuggler all along, and you stopped him.

ending_trapped.title: Ending: Locked In the Light
ending_trapped.text: The fisherman has locked the tower from outside. You and Elena are safe but trapped until the morning ferry spots you. By then the red boat and its cargo are long gone.

notes.text: Through the door, the fisherman laughed. 'Thanks for telling me where to look,' he called. Plot twist: the man you trusted was the one you should have feared.

Through the door, you heard him talk into a radio: 'No fog tonight. We wait for the next one.' Then his steps faded away. The harbor master never came. Plot twist: the harbor was watching for your signal, and you never sent one.
Through the door, he called: 'Whoever you are, nobody knows you're up there.' He was right. You had told no one. Plot twist: by trusting no one, you left no one to come for you.
